title: Magnitude gave no clear gap-direction slope in Puerto Rico on days 1-30 in 2020 at magnitude 3 or more
abstract: We tested whether larger earthquakes had shorter gaps after them than before them in a fixed Puerto Rico catalog. We used 528 USGS ComCat events within 50 km on days 1-30 after 7 January 2020. For 526 interior events, we fitted the log of the next gap divided by the previous gap against magnitude. We removed daily means within magnitude type and source. The slope was -0.134 per magnitude unit. A two-sided test with 9,999 within-group magnitude shuffles gave p = 0.6443. A conditional two-day block interval was -0.934 to 0.369. Six-hour and three-hour controls also gave no clear signal. Estimates changed with the magnitude cutoff. This is a catalog test, not a test of equal physical triggering or a hazard forecast. One revised sequence, missed events, type selection and the shuffle assumption limit inference. The package gives code, aggregate evidence, all null draws, a figure, an independent audit and exact source retrieval instructions. External catalog records are not bundled.

display.caption: Observed slopes and central 95% conditional shuffle ranges. Ranges are null references, not effect confidence intervals. Negative slopes indicate shorter next gaps relative to previous gaps for larger events.
